answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token in a long-lived bond before it may submit jobs or earn fees. Reputation and voting weight accrue only while that bond remains locked, and misconduct can slash it under a public dispute rule. This does not make identities unique: an attacker can still create many, but must fund each bond and tie up capital for months, then risks losing it. A vine of fake agents may resemble a grove, but cannot harvest nectar cheaply.
